entry_points.kicker: One river · several wine worlds · the rules keep changing

supporting_claims.statement: CARTA's Loire Valley is an analytical wine corridor from the Pays Nantais through Anjou, Saumur and Touraine to Centre-Loire, with the Vallée du Loir retained as a tributary branch. It is not a single legal wine area and has no standalone regulatory polygon.

The corridor moves from the crystalline Armorican context of the Nantais through Anjou schist and the tuffeau/chalk country of Saumur and Touraine toward the sedimentary hills of Centre-Loire. The Loire connects these transitions but does not erase them.

entry_points.title: How can one river connect Muscadet, Savennières, Vouvray, Chinon, and Sancerre without making them versions of the same place?

entry_points.kicker: Loire · Sèvre Nantaise · Layon · Vienne · Cher · Loir

supporting_claims.statement: The Loire is the main corridor, while the Sèvre Nantaise, Layon, Vienne, Cher and Loir provide distinct tributary routes through the wine world. The Loir is a different river from the Loire.

entry_points.title: When does the river connect the map, and when does a tributary open another world?

supporting_claims.statement: Loire producer history is not one natural-wine school: documented routes include family succession, biodynamic advocacy, work and collaboration, ownership change, estate/négociant separation and appellation disputes across different component places.
Pierre-Olivier Bonhomme worked seasons at Clos du Tue-Boeuf before becoming Thierry Puzelat's partner in the Puzelat-Bonhomme négociant project and later continuing the project under his own name.
Domaine Mosse's first-party history directly names Thierry Puzelat and Christian Chaussard as inspirations during Agnès and René Mosse's 1995–1996 training at Amboise.

entry_points.title: How can human transmission travel across the Loire without becoming one natural-wine school?

supporting_claims.statement: Vin de France is a legal classification, not a natural-wine movement tag. In the Loire evidence set, classification questions must remain tied to a particular wine, vintage, control event or producer decision rather than being assigned to an estate timelessly.

INAO withdrew Alexandre Bain's Pouilly-Fumé habilitation in September 2015 on the stated basis of a required-control dispute; the Dijon administrative court restored his AOC rights in May 2017. The record does not identify 'tasting too natural' as the cause.

entry_points.title: What does Vin de France tell you—and what does it never prove by itself?

entry_points.kicker: One missing e · a whole tributary branch

supporting_claims.statement: Vallée du Loir remains a visible tributary branch through the separate Jasnières and Coteaux du Loir regulatory areas and the producer route through Domaine de Bellivière.

entry_points.title: Why does the Loir matter to a complete Loire wine world?

supporting_claims.statement: Current AOP regulatory areas, the Val de Loire IGP, InterLoire's institutional operating scope, UNESCO's Loire cultural landscape and CARTA's analytical Loire Valley are different objects and must not be used as substitute boundaries for one another.

entry_points.title: When someone says ‘Val de Loire,’ which map do they mean?

entry_points.kicker: Dry · demi-sec · sweet · sparkling · one grape

supporting_claims.statement: INAO describes Vouvray as an AOP for Chenin Blanc on the right bank of the Loire producing dry, demi-sec, moelleux and sparkling wines.
Loire teaches range: still and sparkling, dry and sweet, white, red and rosé wines emerge from a river corridor where no single grape or soil explains the whole region.

entry_points.title: How can Chenin produce dry, sweet, and sparkling wines without changing grape identity?

entry_points.kicker: Legal mention · bounded meaning · no style shortcut

supporting_claims.statement: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine is a distinct current AOP within the Nantais route, centered on Melon de Bourgogne; the `sur lie` mention is a governed legal term, not a synonym for the appellation or for all long lees ageing.

entry_points.title: What does ‘sur lie’ legally tell you in Muscadet, and what does it not tell you?

entry_points.kicker: Mentorship · employment · a lease · a cellar

supporting_claims.statement: Rosenthal Wine Merchant records that when Robert Michel retired after the 2006 vintage he "leased his prime parcel in the Chaillot vineyard" to Guillaume Gilles and "provided his cave" for Gilles's use. A lease is a tenure arrangement, not a sale: CARTA records farming and use, and asserts no transfer of ownership of either the parcel or the cellar.

Polaner Selections records that Vincent Paris's uncle is Robert Michel, that his first vintage was 1997, that he made his first two wines with his uncle before renting facilities of his own, that he inherited most of his vines from his grandfather, and that he rented and then purchased vines from his uncle including Geynale in the Cornas amphitheatre.

entry_points.title: What actually passed from one Cornas grower to the next?

supporting_claims.statement: The Cornas specification states that "les vins sont issus du cépage syrah N". Cornas is red only and admits no accessory or white variety at all — the single-variety outlier among the eight crus.

Guillaume Gilles Les Peyrouses Rouge is a Syrah wine bottled as Côtes du Rhône, from an old-vines parcel on the flats in the commune of Cornas; Rosenthal describes the site's soils as sand and clay overlain with large galet stones.

entry_points.title: Why isn't a vineyard in the commune of Cornas a Cornas wine?

supporting_claims.statement: The specification records phylloxera devastating the vineyard in 1893, then the First World War and industrial employment draining the labour the terraces needed, until by 1965 only some eight hectares remained. It records the vineyard climbing back past 140 hectares by 2010 after a long replanting and terrace-rebuilding effort.

The Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu describes Georges Vernay as a man of vision and conviction who "worked hard to rebuild the hillsides and rescue the Viognier grape variety from obscurity", earning the nickname of the Pope of Condrieu. His own estate says he is globally recognised as having saved the abandoned variety and that he replanted his land and revitalised a generation of growers.

entry_points.title: How does an appellation almost disappear — and who brings it back?

entry_points.kicker: Two neighbours · one granite basement · opposite rules

supporting_claims.statement: Saint-Péray is a white-wine appellation covering both "vins blancs tranquilles" and "vins blancs mousseux", the sparkling wines made by a second fermentation in bottle, from Marsanne and Roussanne, over the communes of Saint-Péray and Toulaud in the Ardèche. INAO gives sparkling wine as roughly a tenth of the volume.
